data: Small synthetic fixtures only. No downloads, keys, or private data.
accounting_checks: Changing the hedge at constant prices creates no gross price profit and pays trade costs.
Positive funding debits a long position and credits a short position, using the mark-price proxy.
Funding uses the carried coin units before a same-hour entry, flip, or final close.
A position flip pays for the old and new notionals on both legs.
The last row closes all positions once and charges current-price notional.
Without an order, coin units stay fixed and portfolio weights drift with prices.
Open-to-open price changes belong to the carried position.
Cash changes agree with price PnL plus funding minus costs, and returns compound to final equity.
Missing values, invalid prices, partial orders, and swapped weight columns are rejected.
timing_checks: A close shock in row k first affects an order in row k+2.
Orders use only the fixed allowed UTC hours.
The uncertainty gate blocks entries but does not itself close an existing position.
The rolling signal mean and sample standard deviation exclude the current close.
Changing closes from row t-1 onward leaves signals through t-2 and orders and cash ledgers through open t unchanged for all five methods.

resolved_findings.issue: Swapped BTC and ETH weight columns were accepted and silently changed the intended positions.
resolved_findings.fix: The cash ledger now checks that weight columns have the required leg order.

review_limits: These tests check numerical accounting and information timing, not trading profit or market efficiency.
Hourly opens are assumed fills; real spread, depth, queue position, and market impact are not tested.
The funding price is an hourly mark-open proxy, not a reconstruction of exchange fee records.
Margin calls, liquidation, and exchange failure are outside the ledger.
The tests do not certify a full historical data download or all model-selection uncertainty.
